summary: One-time cleanup of the untouched legacy default project: older desktop builds created project default_project (名 默认项目), ten world-model seed papers and an automatic fetch on first launch. app/legacy_cleanup.py (called from build_server after the database opens, source run and desktop alike) deletes exactly that auto-made state in one transaction after writing <db>.pre-legacy-cleanup.bak, only when nothing was ever done in it (no feedback, saved paper, question, note, category, import, keyword, rename, pin history, stored PDF/full text, user-intent setting); anything else leaves the library untouched. Result recorded in settings key legacy_default_cleanup; no migration number; never runs twice.
scope_note: Worktree onboarding-tour, fifth commit. Deletes user-library data, hence critical; the conditions are deliberately conservative.

budget_impact.rationale: Local SQLite work at start-up; no model call, network request or prompt.
budget_impact.before: an untouched legacy default project and seed papers stayed in the library
budget_impact.after: removed once, with a backup file

open_risks: Not independently reviewed (critical class; it deletes data).
Not run on the owner's real old library; only on constructed states in tests (the old first-start state is reconstructed from the migration and ensure_seed_papers, not from a real old file).
The backup file <db>.pre-legacy-cleanup.bak is never deleted automatically and holds the old data.
Conservative by design: an old library where anything was touched (even a downloaded PDF) is left as it is; the owner may delete it by hand.

The check relies on table names and the old first-start shape (default_project, seed_keys_/last_refresh_ settings, profile version note 'initial'); a state written by a build not examined here may be kept rather than cleaned (safe direction).
